context: In the table, “Original tree position” is the zero-based level-order position with empty slots preserved. The root is at position 0. “Compacted index” is the array index after empty slots are skipped. The figure shows only the original tree described below.

The original tree has 10 nodes. Root 1 (position 0) has left child 2 (position 1) and right child 3 (position 2). Node 2 has only a left child, 4 (position 3). Node 3 has left child 6 (position 5) and right child 7 (position 6). Node 4 has left child 8 (position 7) and right child 9 (position 8). Node 6 has only a left child, 12 (position 11), and node 7 has only a right child, 15 (position 14). Nodes 8, 9, 12, and 15 are leaves. The table matches compacted array indices 0 through 9 to the original tree positions.

frames.explanation: Positions 4, 9, 10, 12, and 13 are missing from the original tree. Skipping them gives the compacted array [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 15], moving node 6 from original position 5 to compacted index 4. Applying 2i+2 would incorrectly make 6 at index 4 the right child of node 2 at index 1. In the original tree, 2 has no right child and 6 is the left child of 3. Applying the index formulas throughout the compacted array yields a different tree. Node 1 has left child 2 and right child 3, node 2 has left child 4 and right child 6, and node 3 has left child 7 and right child 8. Node 4 has left child 9 and right child 12. Node 6 has only a left child, 15. The remaining nodes are leaves. This tree has different connections but the same level-order sequence of values. It is derived here and is not drawn in the figure.
frames.title: Level-order array with internal empty slots omitted

result: After internal empty slots are omitted, trees with different connections can have the same level-order sequence of values. This problem arises with internal gaps. In a complete binary tree all empty slots come at the end of the sequence, so omitting them preserves the index mapping.
summary: Removing internal empty slots shifts indices in the compacted level-order array. The same sequence of values can then describe different tree shapes.
